title: Light level and duration of exposure determine the impact of self-luminous tablets on melatonin suppression

findings.antecedent: Exposure to tablet with blue LEDs (40 lux, 470-nm light) for 1 hour
findings.mechanism: Short-wavelength light at 470-nm is maximally effective at suppressing melatonin.
findings.quote: suppression values were significantly different than zero at 00:00 (t(10) = 15.0, p < 0.001)

findings.antecedent: Exposure to tablet with blue LEDs (40 lux, 470-nm light) for 2 hours
findings.mechanism: Short-wavelength light at 470-nm is maximally effective at suppressing melatonin.

findings.antecedent: Exposure to tablet-only (full brightness, ~18 lux) for 1 hour
findings.mechanism: Light level and duration of exposure were insufficient to cause statistically significant melatonin suppression.
findings.quote: Suppression after 1-h exposure to the tablet-only condi-tion was not significantly different than zero (t(10) = 1.80, p = 0.103)

findings.antecedent: Exposure to tablet-only (full brightness, ~16 lux) for 2 hours
findings.mechanism: Increased duration of exposure to short-wavelength light from the tablet-only condition led to statistically significant melatonin suppression.
findings.quote: but was signifi-cantly greater than zero after 2 h of exposure (t(11) = 3.39, p = 0.006).

findings.antecedent: Predicted melatonin suppression (46%) for tablet with blue LEDs for 1 hour (based on CS values)
findings.consequent: Actual measured melatonin suppression (48% ± 4%) for tablet with blue LEDs for 1 hour
findings.mechanism: The human circadian phototransduction model accurately predicts melatonin suppression from light exposure.
findings.quote: The mean ± SEM suppression after 1-hr exposure to the tablet with blue LEDs condition was 48% ± 4%, very close to the predicted values, which was 46%.

findings.antecedent: Predicted melatonin suppression (3%) for tablet-only for 1 hour (based on CS values)
findings.consequent: Actual measured melatonin suppression (7% ± 4%) for tablet-only for 1 hour
findings.mechanism: The human circadian phototransduction model accurately predicts melatonin suppression from light exposure.
findings.quote: Suppression after 1-h exposure to the tablet only condition was 7% ± 4%, again, very close to the model predictions, which was 3%.

stimuli.description: Apple iPad (1st or 2nd generation) set to full brightness, viewed under three conditions: 1) tablet-only, 2) tablet viewed through clear-lens goggles with blue LEDs (40 lux, 470-nm light at cornea), 3) tablet viewed through orange-tinted glasses (dark control, optical radiation <525 nm ≈ 0).

tables.description: Mean ± standard error of the mean (SEM) values for photopic illuminance (lux), circadian light (CLA), circadian stimulus (CS), and measured melatonin suppression (%) for different lighting conditions and exposure durations (1h and 2h).

limitations: The model of human circadian phototransduction by Rea and colleagues only takes into account the absolute SPD of the light source. Variables such as duration of exposure and spatial distribution also need to be added to the model to improve its ability to predict the impact of self-luminous displays on acute melatonin suppression.
